site.method: COMPLETED 2026-07-21. Two-stage derivation, full chain in sources/SITE_DERIVATION.md. Stage 1 (map georeferencing): the ch313 app's own maps (p29 'Vicinity Map' 1:150,000, p37 'Reinvestment Zone Within Vicinity' 1:90,000, agmt Exhibit B p83) all legend the same orange box as 'Project Boundary and Proposed Reinvestment Zone' -- one box, no tighter array polygon exists in any source on disk. Pixel centroid of that box found by color-threshold connected-component detection (p37: 2166,1068 px of 6120x4080). Scale derived from paper math, not eyeballing (170dpi exhibit.py render, 1:90,000 printed scale -> 119.68 px/mile), anchored to OSM-Overpass-confirmed Leesville TX (29.4069038,-97.7449990, node 151462694) -> map-derived box = 29.4526,-97.7497. Cross-validated independently on p29 (different scale 71.8px/mi, different anchor Nixon TX node 151811162 at 29.2696579,-97.7625132) -> 29.4531,-97.7552; the two agree to ~100ft on latitude and ~0.3mi on longitude. Qualitative OSM cross-checks: County Road 102 (Overpass way 15252431) sits ~0.6mi east of the box at a matching latitude band; the LCRA 138kV line (way 15250175) sits ~1.4-2.1mi south, matching the IA's own narrative that the POI/Leesville Substation (IA Exhibit C3, sources/..._p59.png) sits SSE of the generation site, not at the site itself. Stage 2 (imagery confirmation, HIGH-CONFIDENCE override): the s2aws.py chip centered on the stage-1 map-derived point (29.453,-97.751, 3.5km buffer) shows a large graded/racking-row construction footprint sitting almost exactly at frame center by 2026-04 and 2026-07 -- confirming the map derivation was correct to within ~0.5km. The reported lat/lon above is the array footprint's own pixel centroid measured directly off the 2026-07-15 (acq. 2026-07-09) chip (bbox ~x:280-460,y:205-390 of the 700x700px/10m-per-px chip -> offset +200m E, +525m N of chip center -> 29.4577,-97.7489), superseding the map-only estimate. gmaps.py stayed 429-blocked throughout (quota, not transient). Overpass 504'd twice on heavier polygon queries (county-boundary relation, substation search) even after a 10s wait + one retry each; those were treated as misses per convention -- the point/way lookups that mattered (Leesville, Nixon, CR102, LCRA line, Gonzales-county substations) all succeeded. ORCHESTRATOR CROSS-CHECK 2026-07-21: three additional independent corroborations — (1) FCC census geocode of 29.4577,-97.7489 = Gonzales County, matching the queue county for 23INR0231 (and ruling out Cachena Solar SLF 23INR0027, queue county Wilson, whose earlier re-check had misattributed this same footprint to itself); (2) OSM/Overpass shows the only transmission line within 2km is 138kV, matching Hoke's queue poiLocation 'tap 138kV 7595 Deer Creek - 7621 Nixon' (Cachena taps 345kV Elm Creek-Old Hickory; nearest OSM-tagged 345kV is >20km); (3) footprint measures ~1.7x1.5km (~550 ac) in the 2026-07 frame — consistent with 95.29MW Hoke, several times too small for 602MW Cachena. Cachena's findings are being corrected separately.
site.confidence: high — construction footprint visually confirmed at the derived location in Sentinel-2 imagery (2026-04 and 2026-07), corroborating an independent two-map georeference within ~0.5km
site.map_artifacts_note: p29 = vicinity map (district-wide context); p37 = reinvestment zone within vicinity (primary derivation source); agmt_p82 = Exhibit A legal description/parcel table (QSTS Ranch Partnership Ltd, Parcel 1715, 4,185.19ac ranch tract); agmt_p83 = Exhibit B survey map (same box, confirms no tighter polygon exists); puct_p59 = IA Exhibit C3, the POI substation (a distinct feature ~2-3mi SSE of the site). Full chain in sources/SITE_DERIVATION.md.

The Second Amendment's in-service date (2026-04-16) has already passed as of the latest imagery (acq. 2026-07-09), and the site is still visibly mid-construction (graded + racking rows, not a completed array) -- i.e. the contract's OWN most recent schedule has already slipped once, with no Third Amendment on file yet to formalize a new date. That makes the queue's un-contracted 2027-05-08 self-report the more credible near-term estimate, not the stale 2026-08-14 contract date.

Construction pace observed (bare 2025-07 -> fully graded 2026-02 -> racking rows 2026-05 -> larger footprint 2026-07, roughly 5-6 months from bare ground to mid-build) is consistent with a utility-scale solar COD landing in the 9-14-month-from-grading range typical for this project size, i.e. late 2026 through mid-2027 -- bracketing the queue's 2027-05-08 date reasonably well.
